task_3.title: Remove legacy module metadata aliases from attr and attrs
task_3.description: Upgrading to attrs 24.1.0 removes the old module-level packaging metadata aliases from both `attr` and `attrs`, leaving only version access in place. Code that previously read non-version metadata from these modules must switch to Python's package metadata APIs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that applications upgrading to attrs 24.1.0 no longer depend on legacy packaging metadata attributes exposed on the `attr` and `attrs` modules, while preserving continued access to version information through the remaining supported compatibility attributes.

expectation.grounded: In attrs 24.1.0, `attr` and `attrs` must continue to support only `__version__` and `__version_info__` as module-level compatibility metadata. Legacy non-version packaging metadata attributes, including names such as `__title__`, `__copyright__`, `__description__`, `__uri__`, `__url__`, `__author__`, `__email__`, and `__license__`, are no longer available and should behave as unsupported attributes by raising `AttributeError`. Consumers that need package metadata beyond version information should use `importlib.metadata` or the `importlib_metadata` backport instead.
expectation.conceptual: The library should no longer expose general package metadata through the `attr` or `attrs` modules. Only version-related compatibility access should remain available there, and all other package metadata should be obtained through the standard Python metadata interfaces.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress module-level access to `__version__` or `__version_info__` on either `attr` or `attrs`. The breaking change is limited to removal of non-version packaging metadata aliases, and removed aliases should fail as ordinary missing attributes rather than remaining as deprecated shims.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing version lookup behavior intact while removing the obsolete metadata alias surface. Removed metadata names should clearly behave as no longer supported instead of continuing to work in a degraded compatibility mode.

behavior: `attr` and `attrs` no longer expose legacy non-version packaging metadata attributes at module scope.
Accessing removed metadata aliases on either module now raises `AttributeError` immediately.
`__version__` remains available on both modules and returns the installed attrs version string.
`__version_info__` remains available on both modules and returns the corresponding `VersionInfo` derived from the installed attrs version.
Package metadata other than version information must be retrieved through `importlib.metadata` or `importlib_metadata` rather than module-level aliases.
acceptance_criteria: When application code reads `attr.__version__` or `attrs.__version__`, it should still receive the installed attrs version string.
When application code reads `attr.__version_info__` or `attrs.__version_info__`, it should still receive the corresponding version info object for the installed attrs package.
When application code reads removed module metadata aliases such as `__url__`, `__author__`, `__email__`, `__title__`, or `__license__` from `attr` or `attrs`, it should receive `AttributeError`.
When application code needs package metadata beyond version information, it should rely on Python package metadata APIs instead of module-level aliases on `attr` or `attrs`.

task_2.title: Remove dependency on the deprecated provides() validator
task_2.description: The attrs 24.1.0 upgrade removes the previously deprecated built-in zope interface validator `attrs.validators.provides()`. Consumers that relied on that public API must stop importing or calling it and preserve any required interface-validation behavior without depending on the removed validator.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that applications upgrading from attrs 23.2.0 to 24.1.0 no longer depend on the removed `attrs.validators.provides()` validator and continue to enforce any required interface-conformance checks through supported application behavior.

expectation.grounded: In attrs 24.1.0, the public validator API no longer defines or exports `provides` from `attr.validators` / `attrs.validators`. Code must not import or call `provides(interface)`, and it must not rely on attrs to supply the former validator object that checked whether a value provided a requested interface.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, built-in zope interface validation support should be treated as removed. Any feature that still needs interface validation must keep the same user-visible validation outcome without relying on `provides()` being present in attrs.

constraints.grounded: The upgrade should only remove reliance on the deleted `provides` API. It should not alter the behavior of unrelated attrs validators, and callers must not depend on the previous deprecation-warning path because the symbol itself is no longer available.
constraints.conceptual: Removing usage of the deleted validator should not introduce broader validation regressions. Existing validation behavior should remain stable except for the absence of the removed built-in interface validator.

behavior: `attrs.validators.provides()` is no longer part of the public validator surface in attrs 24.1.0.
Calling `provides(interface)` is no longer possible because attrs no longer ships that validator factory.
The former runtime path that created a validator and emitted a deprecation warning is replaced by API absence.
Any interface-conformance checks previously delegated to attrs' built-in `provides` validator must be handled outside that removed API.
acceptance_criteria: When an application is upgraded to attrs 24.1.0, it should not import, access, or configure `attrs.validators.provides()` or `attr.validators.provides` anywhere in its runtime code.

When the application still requires interface-conformance validation for attrs-managed values, it should continue enforcing that contract without depending on a built-in `provides()` validator from attrs.
When the upgrade is applied, unrelated attrs validators used by the application should continue to behave as before.

task_1.title: Require positional instance argument for attrs.evolve
task_1.description: Upgrading attrs from 23.2.0 to 24.1.0 removes the deprecated ability to call attrs.evolve() with the source instance passed as the inst keyword argument. Consumers must pass the instance as the first positional argument, and invalid calls now fail immediately with TypeError instead of warning and continuing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that code using attrs.evolve remains compatible with attrs 24.1.0 by passing the source instance as the first positional argument and no longer relying on the deprecated inst keyword form.

expectation.grounded: In attrs 24.1.0, attrs.evolve supports the source object only as its single positional instance argument. Calls that previously used inst= are no longer accepted and now raise TypeError because the required positional instance argument was not provided. When exactly one positional attrs instance is supplied, attrs.evolve should continue to create a copy with the requested keyword attribute changes applied.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should preserve normal object-copying behavior for attrs.evolve when the instance is passed positionally, while making the old keyword-based calling style invalid. Applications should treat the instance parameter as positional-only and expect incorrect argument counts to fail as errors.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the successful behavior of attrs.evolve for one positional attrs instance plus valid field overrides. Preserve existing observable failures for unsupported usage other than the removed deprecation path, including TypeError for invalid invocation and the documented attrs-specific errors for non-attrs inputs or unsupported attribute changes.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only remove the deprecated keyword calling convention and tighten argument validation. Existing valid evolve calls should keep working the same way, and unrelated error conditions should not be loosened or hidden.

behavior: attrs.evolve now requires the source instance to be provided as a positional argument rather than as inst=.
Calling attrs.evolve with no positional instance argument now fails with TypeError instead of falling back to inst= handling.
Calling attrs.evolve with more than one positional argument fails with TypeError due to invalid positional argument count.
Calling attrs.evolve with one positional attrs instance and valid keyword changes still returns a copied instance with those changes applied.
acceptance_criteria: When attrs.evolve is called with an attrs instance as the first positional argument and valid field overrides, it should return a new instance reflecting those overrides.
When attrs.evolve is called using inst= instead of a positional instance argument, it should fail with TypeError.
When attrs.evolve is called without any positional instance argument, it should fail with TypeError.
When attrs.evolve is called with more than one positional argument, it should fail with TypeError.

task_4.title: Adapt to attrs 24.1.0 generated equality semantics
task_4.description: Upgrading attrs from 23.2.0 to 24.1.0 changes how generated equality methods evaluate fields. Equality is now evaluated as direct per-attribute comparisons instead of tuple comparison, which improves runtime performance but changes results for edge cases where an attribute is the same object by identity yet not equal by value, such as NaN-like values.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs-generated equality reflects the 24.1.0 behavior: compare each equality-participating attribute directly, preserve any configured equality key transformation, and no longer treat identity-only matches such as NaN-like values as equal.

expectation.grounded: For attrs-generated `__eq__`, equality must be decided by chaining per-attribute comparisons with `==` across all attributes that participate in equality. If an attribute defines `eq_key`, the comparison must use the transformed values from that key on both instances. The resulting behavior must differ from tuple-based comparison for values that are identical objects but not equal by value, including NaN-like values.
expectation.conceptual: Equality for attrs classes should be evaluated field by field using the class's declared equality rules, including any configured equality normalization. This should deliver faster comparisons while making results depend on actual value equality rather than object identity in edge cases.

constraints.grounded: Do not change which attributes participate in equality. Do not bypass `eq_key` for fields that define it. Instances with no equality-participating attributes should still compare as equal once the generated equality method applies.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the existing equality contract for which fields matter, while updating only the comparison semantics. The upgrade must not broaden or narrow the set of fields considered equal; it only changes how their equality is evaluated.

behavior: Generated equality now evaluates participating attributes one by one instead of constructing tuples of attribute values.
Attributes with `eq_key` are compared using their transformed values on both sides rather than their raw stored values.
Equality short-circuits on the first participating attribute that does not compare equal.
Values that are the same object by identity but are not equal by value, such as NaN-like values, no longer compare equal merely because both instances reference that same object.
acceptance_criteria: When two attrs instances have equal values for every equality-participating attribute, their generated equality should return true.
When any equality-participating attribute differs by value, their generated equality should return false.
When an equality-participating attribute defines `eq_key`, equality should be determined from the transformed values produced by that key for each instance.
When corresponding equality-participating attributes contain the same NaN-like object or another identity-equal-but-value-unequal object, generated equality should return false.
When an attrs class has no attributes participating in equality, its generated equality should still report instances as equal when that generated method is used.

task_5.title: Handle attrs 24.1.0 decorator deprecations
task_5.description: attrs 24.1.0 deprecates the obsolete `repr_ns` argument and the legacy `hash` argument on attrs class decorators. The upgrade now emits runtime deprecation warnings when those arguments are used, so callers should move to default Python 3 repr behavior and `unsafe_hash` to stay forward-compatible.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 24.1.0 does not rely on deprecated decorator arguments by removing use of `repr_ns` and replacing legacy `hash` configuration with supported `unsafe_hash` behavior, while preserving the intended repr and hash outcomes for attrs-based classes.

expectation.grounded: Usage of `attr.s`/`attrs` should be compatible with attrs 24.1.0 such that explicitly passing `repr_ns` no longer occurs, and explicitly passing `hash` is replaced by `unsafe_hash` where hash-generation control is needed. In 24.1.0, providing a non-`None` `repr_ns` or `hash` argument causes a `DeprecationWarning` during class decoration, and `unsafe_hash` remains the authoritative hash-related option when present.
expectation.conceptual: The application should adopt the current attrs decorator contract for Python 3: class reprs should not depend on the deprecated namespace override, and hash behavior should be configured through the supported API so the upgrade does not introduce deprecation warnings or future compatibility risk.

constraints.grounded: Do not change repr or hash behavior beyond what is required to stop use of deprecated arguments. Nested or otherwise namespaced attrs classes should still present the intended repr output under normal Python 3 behavior. Any existing hash-generation intent must remain intact, and if transitional code encounters both legacy and replacement hash options, `unsafe_hash` continues to take precedence.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve the visible behavior of attrs classes while removing reliance on deprecated options. The upgrade should reduce warning noise and future breakage risk without altering the intended identity, representation, or hashability semantics of supported classes.

behavior: Passing a non-`None` `repr_ns` argument to an attrs class decorator now emits a `DeprecationWarning` at decoration time.
Passing a non-`None` `hash` argument to an attrs class decorator now emits a `DeprecationWarning` and the supported replacement is `unsafe_hash`.
When `unsafe_hash` is provided, it continues to override legacy `hash` configuration.
The deprecations affect runtime upgrade behavior even if class creation otherwise still succeeds.
acceptance_criteria: When attrs-decorated classes are defined under attrs 24.1.0, they should not rely on explicitly passing `repr_ns`.
When attrs-decorated classes require hash-generation configuration, they should use `unsafe_hash` rather than the deprecated `hash` argument.
When the upgraded code defines attrs classes without deprecated decorator arguments, it should not trigger deprecation warnings related to `repr_ns` or `hash`.
When hash behavior is configured through `unsafe_hash`, the resulting class hashability should remain consistent with the prior intended behavior.

task_6.title: Deprecate attrs `hash` in favor of `unsafe_hash` and preserve `make_class` annotations
task_6.description: The 24.1.0 upgrade shifts attrs users away from the legacy `hash` argument toward the PEP 681-aligned `unsafe_hash` option for generated classes, while keeping existing calls working with deprecation warnings. The runtime also makes dynamically generated classes from `make_class()` expose type annotations for attributes that declare a type, improving observable introspection behavior during class generation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 24.1.0 preserves class-generation behavior while surfacing the new public contract: `hash` is deprecated in favor of `unsafe_hash` for attrs-based class builders, and `make_class()` should expose declared attribute types through class annotations.

expectation.grounded: Calls that pass `hash` to `@attr.s`, `@attrs.define`, or `make_class()` should remain accepted in 24.1.0 but emit a `DeprecationWarning` directing users toward `unsafe_hash`. For attrs-based class generation, `unsafe_hash` remains the authoritative option when both names are present. `make_class()` should translate a provided `hash` value into `unsafe_hash` behavior and should populate the generated class's `__annotations__` with entries for attributes whose `type` is not `None`, so later type resolution and runtime introspection can observe those declared types.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, code that still uses the old `hash` option should keep working but clearly signal that callers need to migrate to `unsafe_hash`. Dynamically created attrs classes should also retain visible type metadata for attributes that declare a type so consumers can inspect or resolve those annotations after class creation.

constraints.grounded: The deprecation should not remove current `hash` call sites immediately or change the resulting hash-generation behavior beyond routing through `unsafe_hash`. Warning behavior applies only when `hash` is explicitly provided with a non-`None` value. Annotation population for `make_class()` is limited to attributes with a known declared `type` and should not invent annotations for attributes without one.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be backward-compatible at runtime aside from deprecation signaling, and it should only expose annotation data that the caller already declared. Existing class creation flows should continue to work without requiring immediate rewrites.

behavior: Passing `hash=True` or `hash=False` to attrs class builders now triggers a deprecation warning and preserves behavior through the `unsafe_hash` pathway.
Passing `unsafe_hash` continues to control generated `__hash__` behavior and takes precedence over the deprecated `hash` name.
Passing `hash` to `make_class()` is treated as deprecated input, emits a deprecation warning, and is forwarded as `unsafe_hash` for the generated class.
Classes returned by `make_class()` now expose `__annotations__` entries for attributes whose declared `type` is not `None`.
Typed annotations added by `make_class()` remain available for downstream runtime type resolution mechanisms such as attrs type resolution.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller defines an attrs class with `@attr.s(hash=True)` or `@attrs.define(hash=False)`, class creation should still succeed and should emit a `DeprecationWarning` telling the caller to use `unsafe_hash` instead.
When a caller supplies both `hash` and `unsafe_hash`, the generated hash behavior should follow `unsafe_hash` rather than the deprecated alias.

When a caller creates a class with `make_class(..., hash=...)`, class creation should still succeed, should emit a `DeprecationWarning`, and should behave as though the same value had been passed as `unsafe_hash`.
When `make_class()` receives attributes with declared types, the returned class should expose those declared types through `__annotations__` for each attribute whose type is known.
When an attribute passed to `make_class()` has no declared type, the generated class should not add a synthetic annotation entry for that attribute.

task_8.title: Prefer the attrs namespace in type stubs
task_8.description: The upgrade reorganizes type stubs so editor and type-checker integrations prefer `attrs` as the canonical namespace for core decorators and helpers, while preserving compatibility for existing imports from `attr`. The stubs also adopt modern typing notation without introducing a production runtime behavior change in the provided diff.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the upgraded library presents `attrs` as the preferred public namespace for core decorator and field helpers in editor and static-typing workflows, while keeping existing `attr` imports compatible and preserving runtime behavior.

expectation.grounded: Type stubs should treat `attrs.define`, `attrs.mutable`, `attrs.frozen`, and `attrs.field` as the primary definitions exposed to IDE and type-checker tooling, with `attr.define`, `attr.mutable`, `attr.frozen`, and `attr.field` remaining available through compatibility imports. The shipped stubs should use modern type-annotation syntax, and no production runtime change is evidenced by the provided code diff.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, developers should see `attrs` suggested as the preferred import source for the library's main class/decorator helpers, while older code that imports the same APIs from `attr` continues to work. Typing information should feel up to date, but application behavior should stay the same.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove or break the public ability to access `define`, `mutable`, `frozen`, or `field` through the `attr` namespace. Do not introduce observable runtime behavior changes for these APIs beyond editor and static-analysis improvements implied by the stub reorganization.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must improve typing and import guidance without forcing users to rewrite working code or changing how the library behaves at runtime.

behavior: Editor quick-fix and auto-import flows should prefer the `attrs` namespace for `define`, `mutable`, `frozen`, and `field`.
The same public helpers remain accessible from `attr`, preserving compatibility for existing imports.
Static typing metadata uses modern annotation notation in the published stubs.
No production runtime behavior change is indicated by the provided code diff.
acceptance_criteria: When a developer requests an import quick-fix for `define`, `mutable`, `frozen`, or `field`, the suggested canonical source should be `attrs`.
When existing code imports `define`, `mutable`, `frozen`, or `field` from `attr`, it should remain valid and continue to behave as before.
When tooling reads the distributed type information, it should expose current typing syntax without changing the observable runtime contract of the library.
When upgrading from 23.2.0 to 24.1.0, users should experience a typing/editor integration improvement rather than a runtime feature or behavior change.

task_9.title: Preserve AttributeError for slotted cached_property access
task_9.description: The upgrade fixes attribute lookup behavior for slotted attrs classes that use functools.cached_property so that AttributeError raised during property resolution is preserved instead of being masked by generated fallback handling. This aligns cached property access with normal Python attribute access semantics and avoids turning real property failures into misleading missing-attribute errors.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that slotted attrs classes using functools.cached_property preserve the original AttributeError raised during property access, instead of converting it into a generic missing-attribute failure, and ensure attribute lookup follows normal Python fallback semantics when inherited attribute handlers are present.

expectation.grounded: For attrs classes generated with slots enabled and using functools.cached_property, the generated attribute fallback should first defer to super().__getattribute__(item). If that lookup raises AttributeError, it should only fall back to super().__getattr__(item) when such a handler exists. When the AttributeError originates from the underlying property or inherited attribute access and no fallback __getattr__ resolves it, that same AttributeError should propagate to the caller unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Accessing a cached property on a slotted attrs class should behave like normal Python attribute access: real AttributeError exceptions raised by dependent properties should be surfaced as-is, and fallback lookup should only happen when an actual fallback handler exists.

constraints.grounded: Do not replace an AttributeError raised by inherited __getattribute__ or a property reached during cached_property evaluation with a newly synthesized missing-attribute error. Preserve successful cached_property reads and continue delegating to inherited __getattr__ only when it is actually defined.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must avoid masking real runtime failures while preserving existing successful attribute and cached-property behavior. It should not introduce extra fallback handling for classes that do not define one.

behavior: Accessing functools.cached_property on a slotted attrs class now consults inherited __getattribute__ before attempting inherited __getattr__.
If inherited __getattribute__ raises AttributeError and no inherited __getattr__ exists, that AttributeError is propagated unchanged to the caller.
If inherited __getattribute__ raises AttributeError and an inherited __getattr__ exists, lookup may continue through that fallback handler.
AttributeError raised by a property involved in cached_property resolution is preserved instead of being converted into a generic missing-attribute failure for the slotted instance.
Cached properties that resolve successfully continue to return their computed value normally.
acceptance_criteria: When a slotted attrs class defines a functools.cached_property that reads another property which raises AttributeError, accessing the cached property should raise that original AttributeError.
When a slotted attrs class with functools.cached_property inherits attribute access behavior, attribute resolution should consult inherited __getattribute__ before any inherited __getattr__ fallback.

When inherited attribute lookup raises AttributeError and no inherited __getattr__ fallback exists, the caller should receive that same AttributeError rather than a replacement missing-attribute error.
When an inherited __getattr__ fallback exists and can resolve the attribute, cached property access should continue to work through that fallback path.
When the cached property and any dependent properties resolve successfully, attribute access should continue to return the expected computed value.

task_7.title: Fix slotted cached_property behavior in attrs 24.1.0
task_7.description: The upgrade fixes runtime handling of functools.cached_property on slotted attrs classes so cached-property methods keep the correct class context, support inherited access via super(), and do not retain obsolete class objects after attrs rebuilds the class for slots.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that slotted attrs classes using functools.cached_property behave correctly after class rebuilding: cached properties must support inherited access patterns such as zero-argument super() and must not keep the discarded original class alive.

expectation.grounded: For classes created with attrs slot support, functools.cached_property members must be rebound against the final generated class so cached-property methods that rely on a __class__ closure, including zero-argument super(), resolve correctly. The cached-property attribute access path must not retain the original pre-rewrite class object after the slotted class has been constructed.
expectation.conceptual: Slotted classes with cached properties should behave like normal Python classes for inherited property logic, and the internal slotting process should not leak stale class objects.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing cached-property behavior for slotted attrs classes apart from these fixes: cached properties should still act as cached attributes on access, and names that are not matched as cached properties should continue to follow the class's normal missing-attribute lookup behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Only correct the cached-property inheritance and cleanup issues. Do not change normal caching semantics or unrelated attribute lookup behavior.

behavior: A functools.cached_property defined on a slotted attrs class keeps a valid class closure after attrs rebuilds the class for slots support.
A slotted cached_property can use zero-argument super() to read inherited state or behavior from its base classes.
The cached-property support path no longer holds a lingering reference to the discarded original class object created before slot rewriting.
Missing attributes that are not registered cached properties continue to follow the class's pre-existing missing-attribute handling.
acceptance_criteria: Given a slotted attrs subclass with a functools.cached_property that uses zero-argument super(), when the property is accessed, it should resolve against the inherited class hierarchy and return the computed value without failing because of stale class context.
Given a slotted attrs class that defines functools.cached_property members, when attrs finishes constructing the class, those properties should remain usable as cached attributes on instances.
Given a slotted attrs class with cached properties, when the temporary pre-slotted class object is no longer otherwise referenced, it should be eligible for garbage collection.
When an unrelated missing attribute is requested on a slotted attrs class that also has cached properties, it should continue to follow the class's normal missing-attribute behavior.

task_11.title: Support type resolution for classes generated with attrs.make_class
task_11.description: The upgrade makes dynamically generated attrs classes expose field annotations so later type resolution works consistently, and it moves the legacy make_class hash option onto the unsafe_hash deprecation path.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that classes created with `attrs.make_class()` preserve declared field types in a way that allows later type resolution to work on the generated class, while continuing to accept the legacy hashing option with the library's deprecation behavior.

expectation.grounded: `attrs.make_class()` should populate the generated class's `__annotations__` mapping for attributes whose `attr.ib()` or `attrs.field()` declaration provides a non-`None` type. Calling `attrs.resolve_types()` on that generated class should then be able to resolve those annotations, including forward-reference string types, into the corresponding field metadata. When `make_class(..., hash=...)` is used, the call should emit a `DeprecationWarning` and behave through `unsafe_hash` compatibility rather than failing.
expectation.conceptual: Dynamically created attrs classes should behave like normally declared classes for type-aware consumers: typed fields remain discoverable on the class, deferred type resolution can resolve declared types afterward, and older hashing configuration continues to work only through a deprecation path.

constraints.grounded: Only fields with an explicitly declared, non-`None` type should appear in the generated class annotations. Untyped fields must remain absent from `__annotations__`. The update must preserve `attrs.resolve_types()` compatibility for generated classes without requiring users to redefine fields manually. Use of the legacy `hash` argument must warn instead of silently changing semantics or raising a new runtime error.
constraints.conceptual: The change should add missing annotation visibility without inventing types for untyped fields or breaking existing generated-class behavior. Backward compatibility should be maintained for older hashing usage, but users should receive a clear deprecation signal.

behavior: `attrs.make_class()` now attaches a `__annotations__` dictionary to the generated class based on declared field types.
Fields declared without a usable type are omitted from the generated class annotations.
Running `attrs.resolve_types()` on a class returned by `attrs.make_class()` can now resolve declared annotations, including string-based forward references, into the field type metadata.
Passing the `hash` argument to `attrs.make_class()` triggers a `DeprecationWarning` and is translated to `unsafe_hash` behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a class is created with `attrs.make_class()` and one or more fields declare explicit types, the generated class should expose those typed fields in `__annotations__`.
When a generated attrs class contains string-based type declarations and `attrs.resolve_types()` is called, the corresponding field metadata should reflect the resolved runtime types afterward.
When fields in `attrs.make_class()` do not declare a type, they should not appear in the generated class annotations solely because the class was created dynamically.
When existing code calls `attrs.make_class(..., hash=...)`, it should continue to run but emit a `DeprecationWarning` instead of behaving as a newly unsupported API.

task_12.title: Add disjunctive attrs validator composition
task_12.description: The upgrade adds `attrs.validators.or_()` as a new public validator combinator so attribute validation can accept values that satisfy any one of several validators instead of requiring all of them to pass. This enables direct OR-style validation semantics, including nested compositions, and defines the failure mode when no alternative matches.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that applications using attrs can declare a single validator that accepts an attribute value when any one of multiple alternative validators succeeds, and rejects the value only when none of the alternatives are satisfied.

expectation.grounded: Expose `attrs.validators.or_(*validators)` as a public validator combinator. The returned validator must invoke its wrapped validators against the same attribute value until one validator completes successfully, then treat the composite validation as successful. If every wrapped validator fails, the composite validator must raise `ValueError`. Nested `or_` compositions should behave as one combined OR validator over all wrapped validators.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to model alternative valid shapes for one attribute with a built-in OR validator. A value should be accepted if it matches at least one allowed validation rule, and rejected only when it matches none of them.

constraints.grounded: The composite validator must not require all wrapped validators to pass. Exceptions raised by failing branches must not stop evaluation of later branches if a later validator can still accept the value. The overall failure signal for the composite must remain a `ValueError` when no branch succeeds.
constraints.conceptual: The new validator must preserve OR semantics: one successful branch is enough, later alternatives must still be considered after earlier failures, and complete failure must surface as a single validation error from the composite.

behavior: `attrs.validators.or_()` returns one validator object that evaluates multiple validators as alternatives.
The composite validator stops at the first wrapped validator that accepts the value and treats the overall validation as successful.
If all wrapped validators reject the value, the composite validator raises `ValueError`.
Failures from earlier wrapped validators are suppressed while other alternatives remain available to evaluate.
Supplying an existing `or_` validator to `or_()` is flattened so nested OR compositions behave like one combined alternative set.
acceptance_criteria: When an attribute uses `attrs.validators.or_()` with multiple validators and the value satisfies any one of them, the attribute validation should succeed.
When the first alternative fails but a later alternative succeeds, the composite validator should still accept the value.
When every alternative fails for the same value, the composite validator should raise `ValueError`.
When nested OR validator compositions are combined, the resulting validator should accept and reject values according to the full set of alternatives rather than treating nested groups differently.

task_10.title: Add context-aware wrapped converters for attrs fields
task_10.description: The upgrade introduces a public converter wrapper API that allows attrs field converters to receive the partially initialized instance and/or the current field definition during value conversion. Conversion behavior is updated consistently across normal initialization paths, including composed converters created with attr.converters.pipe(), while plain one-argument converters remain supported.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs users can define field converters that optionally receive the instance being initialized and the current field definition, so conversion logic can depend on object state or field metadata during initialization.

expectation.grounded: Expose `attr.Converter` and `attrs.Converter` as public APIs for wrapping a converter callable with `takes_self` and `takes_field` options. When such a wrapped converter is supplied to `attr.field` or equivalent field declarations, attrs should call it with the incoming value first, and then pass the partially initialized instance and/or the field's `Attribute` object according to those flags. Existing plain converter callables must still be accepted. Conversion should continue to run for initialized values as well as values coming from defaults or factories. `attr.converters.pipe()` should participate in the wrapper-based converter model and return a `Converter` object rather than a bare callable. The release note also indicates that static type checker support for these wrapped converters is not yet available.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to opt into richer field conversion by wrapping a converter so it can see the object under construction and the field definition. This richer conversion must work anywhere attrs normally performs conversion during initialization, without breaking existing simple converters. Converter composition through `attr.converters.pipe()` should remain usable under the new model, but the feature should be treated as a runtime capability rather than a statically typed one.

constraints.grounded: Do not require users to rewrite existing one-argument converters. Additional conversion context is opt-in and only applies when the converter is wrapped in `Converter`. The wrapped converter's extra arguments are positional and are limited to the current instance and the current `Attribute` definition. Behavior must remain consistent across initialization paths that assign directly or via attrs' generated setter logic. Public consumers should not need internal implementation details to use the feature.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must preserve backward compatibility for existing converter usage while adding optional context-aware conversion. The new behavior should be observable only through supported public APIs and normal object construction, without forcing any particular implementation strategy or depending on internal class layout details.

behavior: A new public `Converter` wrapper type is available from both `attr` and `attrs`.
Wrapped converters can declare whether they receive the partially initialized instance, the field definition, or both, in addition to the value being converted.
Attrs initialization uses wrapped converters when converting explicit constructor inputs, defaulted values, and factory-produced values.
If a field still uses a plain converter callable instead of `Converter`, attrs treats it as a normal single-argument converter.
`attr.converters.pipe()` now returns a `Converter` object instead of a plain callable so composed conversion can participate in the wrapper-based conversion flow.

Initializer argument type inference continues to use the wrapped converter callable's first parameter annotation when available, but the release note explicitly warns that type checkers do not yet support the new self/field-aware converter form.
acceptance_criteria: When a field uses `attr.Converter(..., takes_self=True)`, instantiating the attrs class should invoke the converter with the field value and the partially initialized instance.
When a field uses `attr.Converter(..., takes_field=True)`, instantiating the attrs class should invoke the converter with the field value and the field's `Attribute` definition.
When both `takes_self` and `takes_field` are enabled, instantiating the attrs class should provide both pieces of context in addition to the value being converted.
When a field uses an unwrapped converter callable, initialization should continue to perform standard single-argument conversion with no required code changes from users.
When conversion is triggered from a default value or a factory result instead of a caller-supplied argument, the same wrapped-converter semantics should still apply.
When users build a composed converter with `attr.converters.pipe()`, the resulting object should be usable as a field converter under the new wrapper-based API.

task_13.title: Fix attrs pre-init handling for keyword-only defaults
task_13.description: The upgrade fixes an attrs initialization bug where classes could fail when a parameterized __attrs_pre_init__ is used together with a keyword-only field that has a default value. Generated initialization now forwards keyword-only values correctly so construction succeeds and pre-init sees the resolved value.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs-based classes can be instantiated when __attrs_pre_init__ accepts arguments and a field combines keyword-only initialization with a default value, without crashing and while making the resolved keyword-only value available during pre-init.

expectation.grounded: For attrs-generated __init__ or __attrs_init__, when a class defined with attr.define or equivalent has attr.field(kw_only=True, default=...) and implements __attrs_pre_init__ with arguments, attrs should invoke __attrs_pre_init__ with the same logical initializer inputs, including keyword-only fields passed by name. A defaulted keyword-only field should contribute its resolved value to the pre-init call instead of breaking initializer generation or object construction.
expectation.conceptual: Classes that use attrs pre-initialization hooks should continue to work even when some constructor inputs are keyword-only and optional. If a keyword-only value is omitted, normal default resolution should happen and pre-init should observe that resolved value.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve keyword-only constructor semantics for attrs fields, keep __attrs_pre_init__ argument passing aligned with initializer inputs, and avoid regressions for classes that already work with positional fields, keyword-only fields without defaults, or parameterless __attrs_pre_init__ methods.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to correcting initialization behavior for the failing combination and must not alter the normal calling pattern for other attrs-based constructors.

behavior: Attrs-generated initializers continue to expose keyword-only fields as keyword-only constructor parameters.
When __attrs_pre_init__ accepts arguments, attrs forwards keyword-only field values into that hook by keyword name rather than mixing in default expressions from the initializer signature.
If a keyword-only field has a default and the caller omits it, initialization succeeds and __attrs_pre_init__ receives the resolved default value for that field.
If the caller provides an explicit value for the keyword-only field, that provided value is the one forwarded into __attrs_pre_init__.
acceptance_criteria: When an attrs class defines a keyword-only field with a default and __attrs_pre_init__ declares that field as a keyword-only argument, constructing the class without supplying the field should succeed and pre-init should receive the defaulted value.
When the same class is constructed with an explicit keyword-only value, construction should succeed and pre-init should receive the explicit value.

When attrs generates __init__ or __attrs_init__ for a class that combines parameterized __attrs_pre_init__, keyword-only fields, and defaults, the generated initializer should remain callable and should not crash because of that combination.

task_14.title: Keep attrs.validators.in_() usable with mutable option collections
task_14.description: Upgrading to attrs 24.1.0 changes attrs.validators.in_() so validators created from list, dict, or set options remain hashable while preserving the original allowed options in user-visible validation output and introspection. This removes failures in attrs features that depend on hashable validator metadata without changing the allowed-value contract.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that fields using attrs.validators.in_() remain usable in attrs workflows that require hashable validator metadata even when the allowed options are provided as a list, dict, or set, while validation continues to reflect the original allowed options seen by users.

expectation.grounded: attrs.validators.in_(options) should continue to validate with the same membership contract as value-in-options, but when options is a list, dict, or set the resulting validator must remain hashable. Validation failures must still raise ValueError for disallowed values, and the expected options surfaced through the validator's public representation and failure payload should reflect the original caller-provided options rather than an internal normalized form.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to define an in_ validator from common mutable collections without breaking other attrs features that inspect or filter fields. The validator should still behave like the same allowed-values check, and any visible error or introspection output should describe the options the user originally supplied.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable acceptance rule for attrs.validators.in_(): values are still accepted or rejected according to membership in the supplied options, including key membership for dict inputs. Keep the public failure mode as ValueError for invalid values, and preserve user-facing reporting of the original options instead of exposing internal tuple normalization.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should remove compatibility problems caused by unhashable option collections without changing what values are considered valid or making diagnostics look like a different set of allowed options.

behavior: attrs.validators.in_() now normalizes list, dict, and set option collections into a hashable internal form so the validator itself can participate in attrs operations that require hashability.
The validator still applies the same membership-based validation semantics as the supplied options, including dict key membership behavior.
If validation fails, the raised ValueError should identify the original allowed options supplied by the user rather than an internal normalized tuple.
The validator's public representation should continue to display the original caller-provided options, not the hashability-preserving internal storage form.
acceptance_criteria: When a field uses attrs.validators.in_() with a list, set, or dict of allowed options, attrs features that require hashable validator or field metadata should be able to operate on that field without failing because the validator is unhashable.
When a value is not allowed by attrs.validators.in_(), the field validation should raise ValueError and report the original allowed options as the expected domain.
When the validator is inspected or rendered for debugging, it should show the same options object shape the user originally supplied rather than exposing an internal tuple conversion.
When options are supplied in a form that already works with membership checks, upgrading should not change which values pass or fail validation.

task_15.title: Support inherited __attrs_init_subclass__ hooks
task_15.description: Upgrade to attrs 24.1.0 so attrs-decorated subclasses can use an inherited __attrs_init_subclass__ hook as a post-class-assembly initialization point. This enables subclass registration and similar subclass setup patterns to run against the final assembled class for both slotted and non-slotted attrs classes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs-decorated subclasses invoke an inherited __attrs_init_subclass__ hook after class creation is complete, so subclass registration and other post-assembly setup logic works consistently.

expectation.grounded: For classes built with attrs, if a subclass inherits a __attrs_init_subclass__ class method from a base class, attrs should call that hook exactly once after the subclass has been fully assembled. The hook should run against the final subclass object, including attrs-generated class shape, and should behave consistently for slotted and non-slotted attrs classes. This hook is the attrs-specific replacement for relying on Python's __init_subclass__ during attrs class construction.
expectation.conceptual: Applications using attrs should be able to define subclass-initialization logic once on a base class and have it automatically run for each derived attrs class after the derived class is ready. This should make class registration and similar subclass lifecycle behavior work reliably without depending on incomplete class state.

constraints.grounded: Do not change class creation behavior for attrs classes that do not inherit __attrs_init_subclass__. Preserve normal attrs class construction semantics while adding the post-assembly hook call, and keep the hook scoped to inherited __attrs_init_subclass__ behavior rather than introducing unrelated subclass-initialization side effects.
constraints.conceptual: The new capability should be additive and narrowly targeted. Existing attrs class creation should continue to behave the same unless a project opts into the subclass hook pattern.

behavior: An attrs-decorated subclass that inherits __attrs_init_subclass__ from a base class triggers that hook after the subclass has finished attrs class assembly.
The inherited hook is invoked once per subclass creation and receives the completed subclass as its class context.
Subclass-initialization behavior via __attrs_init_subclass__ works for both slotted and non-slotted attrs classes.
Projects can use __attrs_init_subclass__ for observable post-creation actions such as maintaining subclass registries.
acceptance_criteria: When a base attrs class defines __attrs_init_subclass__ and a derived attrs class is declared, the derived class should cause that hook to run exactly once.
When the inherited hook records or registers subclasses, the newly declared attrs subclass should appear in that registration as the final assembled class.
When the same subclass-initialization pattern is used with slots enabled, it should behave the same as with non-slotted attrs classes.
When an attrs class hierarchy does not use an inherited __attrs_init_subclass__ hook, class creation should continue without new observable side effects.
